item.title: Listen to an accessibility test debrief
item.summary: A campus team discovers why maps that passed a desk review still confused visitors.
item.transcript_text:
Coordinator: We tested the printed campus maps with new visitors. Most could identify the building by name, but several took the long route around it.
Designer: Did the maps show the steps at the south entrance?
Coordinator: They showed steps, but the symbol for the lift was inside the building. People treated that as proof they could enter from the south and use it. In reality, the north entrance is the step-free one.
Designer: Let's mark the approach as well as the lift. We should test both a printed map and the web version outdoors.
Coordinator: And give people a real task. Ask them to reach a room, rather than tell us whether the symbol makes sense.

questions.prompt: What did the map test chiefly reveal?
options: Visitors cannot read any symbol outdoors
Finding a building and finding a usable route are different tasks
Web maps always work better indoors
Building names should be replaced with numbers
questions.explanation: The visitors could identify the building but misconstrued how to enter it.

questions.prompt: Why did some visitors think the south entrance would work?
options: They saw a lift marked inside the building
The map claimed the steps had been removed
The north entrance had no label
A visitor guide told them to go south
questions.explanation: The lift symbol suggested a step-free connection that did not exist from the south.

questions.prompt: What change does the designer propose?
options: Remove all symbols from the printed map
Test the outdoor route with staff only
Move the entrance to the south side
Show the route to the step-free entrance
questions.explanation: The designer wants to mark the approach as well as the lift.

questions.prompt: Where should the next comparison be done?
options: In a print shop
Inside the lift
Outdoors
In a classroom with staff
questions.explanation: The designer proposes comparing both versions outside.

questions.prompt: Why is a real wayfinding task preferred?
options: It avoids discussing any design decisions
It shows whether visitors can use the map to get there
It is the fastest way to identify all visitors
It removes the need to print maps
questions.explanation: The coordinator distinguishes successful navigation from opinions about a symbol.
